## What it is

Firefly III keeps track of your money: accounts, transactions, budgets, categories, bills and reports, using double-entry bookkeeping ([firefly-iii/firefly-iii](https://github.com/firefly-iii/firefly-iii)).

**Licence:** `AGPL-3.0` (GitHub licence API; license-matrix row "Firefly III"). Market class **L2**.

**Icon:** a neutral generated icon with initials; no upstream logo is shipped.

## Market listing

- Category and sub-tags (docs/design/TAXONOMY.md §1): finance: budget. The sub-tags go into `metadata.tags` once the schema has it.
- Deployment class (TAXONOMY §2): **Market · community** until CI writes a passing scan (contract §9.4), then Market · verified if every check passes.

## How it runs here

- One `Deployment` (`Recreate`) with the app (`fireflyiii/core`, nginx and PHP-FPM, as `www-data`, UID 33) and PostgreSQL 18 as a native sidecar that listens on 127.0.0.1 only. PostgreSQL trusts local connections, so there is no database password and no Secret. Upstream's compose file uses MariaDB; Firefly III supports PostgreSQL (`DB_CONNECTION=pgsql` in `.env.example`).
- `APP_KEY` (exactly 32 characters, required) is generated once by an init container onto the data volume and read through `APP_KEY_FILE`. It is never committed and is not visible in the manifests.
- Volumes: `firefly-iii-data` (5 GiB: attachments and the key) and `firefly-iii-db` (5 GiB).
- Probes: `GET /healthcheck` (the image's own health path); startup allows 10 minutes for migrations.
- All containers run non-root, no privilege escalation, all capabilities dropped.

## First run

Source: [docs.firefly-iii.org](https://docs.firefly-iii.org/) (installation, Docker).

1. Install Firefly III from the Market and approve the action. It installs into `app-firefly-iii`.
2. Forward the port and open http://localhost:8080:
   ```sh
   kubectl -n app-firefly-iii port-forward svc/firefly-iii 8080:8080
   ```
3. Register the first user right after install: the first account becomes the owner.
4. Keep the data volume in your backups: without the generated `APP_KEY` the encrypted fields in the database cannot be read.

## Not done yet

- The daily cron job (recurring transactions, bills, auto-budgets: `php artisan firefly-iii:cron`) is not scheduled yet. Until a CronJob is added, run it by hand: `kubectl -n app-firefly-iii exec deploy/firefly-iii -c firefly-iii -- php artisan firefly-iii:cron`.
- The Data Importer (bank imports) is a separate upstream app and is not packaged.
- No email (SMTP) settings: password reset mails are not sent.
- No HTTPS or LAN hostname: OneMind v0 has no ingress or certificates for apps, so the web UI is reached through a port-forward until the app proxy exists. `APP_URL` matches that port-forward.
- `readOnlyRootFilesystem` is not set: it has not been tested against this image.
- Resource figures are OneMind choices; upstream publishes none. They are checked against real use when the CI smoke test (contract §9.4 check 9) runs.
- `metadata.tier` stays `community` until `sdk/tools/app-gate` in CI writes a passing `scan.json`. `spec.updates.automerge` is `none` until `renovate.json` lists the app.

## Why this app is blocked

The CI app gate (`sdk/tools/app-gate`, contract §9.4) computed tier **blocked** for this app on 2026-11-12 (ci-apps run 43212771377, job `gate (firefly-iii)`). The gateway lists a blocked app in the Market but refuses to install it (§10.3, §11.1). The app is kept, not hidden, and the gate was not weakened. Reasons from that run:

- Vulnerability: `docker.io/fireflyiii/core:version-6.7.9`: CVE-2026-111497 in `libbrotli1` 1.1.0-2+b7 (fixed 1.1.0-2+deb13u1); CVE-2026-99083 in `linux-libc-dev` 6.12.113-1 (fixed 6.12.115-2).
- Vulnerability: `docker.io/library/postgres:18.6-trixie`: CVE-2025-68121 in the Go `stdlib` v1.24.6 (fixed 1.24.13, 1.25.7, 1.26.0-rc.3).
- Secret finding (Trivy): the postgres image has `private-key` (HIGH) in `/etc/ssl/private/ssl-cert-snakeoil.key` (Debian's ssl-cert package).
- Passed: licence AGPL-3.0 (matrix row matches), ClamAV (0 infected), smoke test (GET / returned 302).

To unblock: move the pins to upstream releases that fix these findings (tags that exist, checked with `crane`), then rerun `sdk/tools/app-gate` (the daily `apps-rescan` workflow does this too). Nothing is bumped to an unverified tag.
